companies.latest_signal: Core local commerce swung back to an RMB5.7bn operating profit in Q2 2026 (7.9% margin vs 5.7% a year earlier) as on-demand delivery unit economics turned positive and subsidies were meaningfully cut; management (incl. Wang Xing) said industry-wide subsidy levels are still above 2024 norms and full normalization will take several more quarters.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: Quick commerce (Taobao Instant Commerce/Ele.me) EBITA loss
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not disclose a standalone instant-commerce EBITA line — it only reports China E-Commerce Group adjusted EBITA (Taobao/Tmall + instant commerce combined) and group-level adjusted EBITA, both of which management explicitly attributes most of the y/y decline to quick-commerce subsidy investment. Standalone loss figures below are sell-side (CICC/中金) estimates built from that commentary plus management's per-order-loss disclosures, cited by 36kr/Sina/Caixin-adjacent outlets — not a company-reported line item

periods.src: CICC estimate cited in 36kr/Sina coverage of Alibaba FY2026 Q2 (Jul-Sep 2025) results; group adjusted EBITA fell 78% to RMB9.07bn that quarter
CICC estimate cited in Sina/Guancha coverage of Alibaba FY2026 Q3 (Oct-Dec 2025) results
Sell-side estimate range (described as lowest of trailing 4 quarters) cited in Chinese financial press covering Alibaba FY2026 Q4 (Jan-Mar 2026) results; group adjusted EBITA fell 84% to RMB5.1bn

No clean absolute figure disclosed; Alibaba FY2027 Q1 (Apr-Jun 2026, 'June Quarter 2026') results/call reported China Commerce Group adjusted EBITA of RMB39.7bn and total group adjusted EBITA down 30% YoY to RMB27.3bn, with management citing quick-commerce investment as the main drag (Nikkei Chinese, Alibaba IR release)

companies.latest_signal: On the June-quarter 2026 call management said per-order loss in quick commerce was cut roughly 50% versus the July-August 2025 peak, with non-beverage orders over 75% of volume and AOV up double digits — but it also flagged the September 2026 quarter as the likely peak reinvestment period and said the RMB380bn three-year capex/investment plan 'may prove too small,' implying losses could widen again before resuming their decline.

companies.latest_signal: New Businesses operating loss narrowed again to RMB9.85bn in Q2 2026 (from RMB10.35bn in Q1), with CFO Sandy (Shan) Su stating JD Food Delivery cut losses by more than 50% y/y via lower per-order subsidies and better delivery efficiency/commission and ad revenue; CEO Sandy Xu called it an 'inflection point' and management guided to substantial further y/y loss narrowing for JD Food Delivery in H2 2026.

war_summary: Subsidy intensity peaked around Q3 2025 (Meituan core local commerce -RMB14.1bn, JD new businesses -RMB15.7bn, Alibaba's quick-commerce EBITA drag an estimated -RMB36.7bn) under explicit regulator pressure (SAMR-led 'anti-involution'/反内卷 campaigns) to curb irrational per-order subsidies; by Q2 2026 Meituan and JD have both clearly de-escalated and returned toward/into profit, while Alibaba is the holdout still reinvesting heavily behind Taobao Instant Commerce/Ele.me and has flagged the Jul-Sep 2026 quarter as a fresh peak-spend period, meaning Alibaba — backed by its 2029 EBITA-breakeven timeline and 'absolute No.1' GMV ambition — looks the least likely of the three to blink first even as Meituan and JD treat the price war as largely over.
